YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cq-7lFMNESk&t=1s
Title: How to setup the desktop Figma MCP server in your code editors
Channel: Figma
Duration: 140 seconds

==== YOUTUBE TRANSCRIPT (AUTO-GENERATED) ====

Bring your design system and Figma file context into your Agentic development tools with the Figma MCP server. This is a powerful way to align your code with your design specifications, and it's easy to enable. We'll walk you through how to set up the Figma MCP local server in this video. First, let's enable the local MCP server in the Figma desktop app. Open the Figma desktop app and make sure you've updated to the latest version. Create or open a Figma design file. With nothing selected on the canvas, switch to dev mode. In the right inspect sidebar, you'll see an MCP server section where you can enable the MCP server. You should see a confirmation message at the bottom of the screen letting you know the server is enabled and running. Click copy URL to copy the address and keep it handy for your configuration file in the next step. Now, let's walk through how to add the Figma MCP server to your development tools. We'll start with cursor. Open the command pallet and search for cursor settings. Click on the MCP and integrations tab and then click add custom MCP. Enter the following configuration or copy it from the Figma help center. [Music] Then save the file and head back to settings. You should see the Figma MCP tool enabled in cursor. Now let's talk about VS Code. Make sure you have GitHub Copilot enabled on your account to use the MCP server. Open the command pallet and search for MCP add server. Select HTTP. Then paste the server URL in the search bar. Then hit enter. Type in Figma MCP when it asks for a server ID. Then hit enter. Select whether you want to add this server globally or only for the current workspace. Once confirmed, you'll see a configuration file like this in your MCP.json file. Finally, we'll set up the MCP server and cloud code. Open your terminal and run the MCP ad command for the cloud CLI. Restart Cloud Code if it was running. You should then see newly available Figma slash commands as well as the Figma MCP server and your /mcp command. Trying to set up the Figma MCP server on other code editors? Check out our help center to learn more.
